extracted.intended_audience: auditors performing A-133 Single Audits of recipients and subrecipients of Federal awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and suggested audit procedures for testing compliance with Federal award requirements (A-102 Common Rule, OMB Circular A-110, program regulations) across multiple compliance areas (cash management, Davis-Bacon, eligibility, property, matching/LOE/earmarking, period of availability, procurement, program income).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of Federal cash draws (Treasury-State Agreement/Subpart B)
rubrics_metrics.description: The timing of the Federal cash draws were in compliance with the applicable funding techniques specified in the Treasury-State Agreement or Subpart B procedures (31 CFR sections 205.7 and 205.20).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a sample of Federal cash draws and verify timing compliance with the Treasury-State Agreement or Subpart B procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbursement of program income/rebates/refunds before additional draws
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent available, program income, rebates, refunds, and other income and receipts were disbursed before requesting additional Federal cash draws as required by the A-102 Common Rule (§_.21) and OMB Circular A-110 (§_.22).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select samples of draws and verify that program income and similar receipts were disbursed prior to requesting further Federal cash draws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement requests supported by documentation of payment prior to request
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a sample of reimbursement requests and trace to supporting documentation showing that the costs for which reimbursement was requested were paid prior to the date of the reimbursement request (31 CFR section 205.7(c)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test reimbursement requests against supplier invoices, cancelled checks or other evidence that costs were paid prior to reimbursement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of interest obligation on Federal cash draws
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the calculation of the interest obligation owed to or by the Federal Government, reported on the annual report submitted by the State to ascertain that the calculation was in accordance with Treasury regulations and the terms of the Treasury-State Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace amounts used in the calculation to supporting documentation and verify calculations conform to Treasury regulations and agreement terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subrecipient procedures to minimize time between transfer and payout (A-102 §.37(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: For programs where Federal cash draws are passed through to subrecipients: select a representative sample of subrecipients and ascertain the procedures implemented to assure that subrecipients minimize the time elapsing between the transfer of Federal funds from the recipient and the payout of funds for program purposes (A-102 Common Rule §.37(a)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review subrecipient procedures and test representative samples for implementation and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subrecipient Federal cash draws conform to procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a representative sample of Federal cash draws by subrecipients and ascertain that they conformed to the procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample draws and document conformity with established procedures to minimize draw-to-disbursement time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for advances to minimize draw-to-payout time
rubrics_metrics.description: For programs which received advances of Federal funds, ascertain the procedures established with the Federal agency or pass-through entity to minimize the time between the transfer of Federal funds and the payout of funds for program purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain and evaluate agreements/procedures between recipient and awarding or pass-through agency regarding advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Established procedures followed to minimize drawdown-to-disbursement time
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a sample of Federal cash draws and verify that established procedures to minimize the time elapsing between drawdown and disbursement were followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test selected draws for compliance with the entity's procedures; include checks that available program income was used first when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest earned on Federal cash draws returned to appropriate agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Review records to determine if interest was earned on Federal cash draws. If so, review evidence to ascertain whether it was returned to the appropriate agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect financial records and evidence of remittance to awarding agencies as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Davis-Bacon Act coverage for construction contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: When required by the Davis-Bacon Act, DOL implementation, or by Federal program legislation, all laborers and mechanics employed by contractors or subcontractors to work on construction contracts in excess of $2000 financed by Federal assistance funds must be paid wages not less than the prevailing wage rates established for the locality by the DOL (40 USC 276a to 276a-7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ascertain whether the non-Federal entity receives Federal funds for construction projects and whether projects are covered by Davis-Bacon requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required prevailing wage clauses in construction contracts/subcontracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a sample of construction contracts and subcontracts and verify that the required prevailing wage rate clauses were included in contracts for construction which exceed $2,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine contract language to confirm inclusion of Davis-Bacon clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine applicable prevailing wage rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the prevailing wage rates applicable at the time of the construction payroll. (DOL's Wage and Hour Division publishes a Register of Wage Determinations.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use DOL publications and online wage determination sources (e.g., FedWorld) to identify applicable rates for the locality and time period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine contractor/subcontractor payrolls and certifications for prevailing wage compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine a sample of contractor or subcontractor payroll submissions and certifications and ascertain if such submissions indicate that laborers and mechanics were paid the prevailing wage rates established by the DOL for the locality at the time of the construction payroll.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare certified payrolls to wage determinations, check with withholding records, and validate payroll certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility determinations made and documented for individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether required eligibility determinations were made (including obtaining any required documentation/verifications) and that individual program participants or groups of participants were determined to be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a sample of individuals receiving benefits and test that required eligibility determinations and documentation exist for initial and continuing eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subawards only to eligible subrecipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Subawards were made only to eligible subrecipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test a sample of awards to subrecipients for evidence of eligibility and compliance with applicable eligibility criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amounts provided to eligibles calculated in accordance with program requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Amounts provided to or on behalf of eligibles were calculated in accordance with program requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For sampled beneficiaries, verify benefit calculations and that payments conform to program rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit and test computer systems integral to eligibility determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: When a computer system is used for processing individual eligibility determinations and delivery of benefits, auditors should follow generally accepted auditing standards and consider the non-Federal entity's computer processing; tests of the computer systems may be performed as part of testing internal controls for eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider system functions (calculations, payments, record maintenance, matches, access controls, exception reports) and test as necessary to support opinion on compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of beneficiary records/database
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform procedures to ascertain if the non-Federal entity's records/database includes all individuals receiving benefits during the audit period (i.e., that the population of individuals receiving benefits is complete).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use data reconciliations, exception testing, and system reports to evaluate completeness of beneficiary populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits discontinued at end of eligibility period
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefits were discontinued when the period of eligibility expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample records to verify timely cessation of benefits when eligibility periods end and redeterminations were performed where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of quality control processes for eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: In some programs, the non-Federal entity is required to use a quality control process to obtain assurances about eligibility. Review the quality control process and perform tests to ascertain if it is operating effectively and in compliance with applicable program requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of quality control procedures and test their outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility testing for groups or areas of service delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: When eligibility is determined for a population or area of service delivery, test information used in determining eligibility and ascertain if the population or area of service delivery was eligible and benefits were calculated correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform tests of documentation and calculations used to support group/area eligibility determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for subrecipients based on approved applications/plans
rubrics_metrics.description: If the determination of eligibility is based upon an approved application or plan, obtain a copy of this document and identify the applicable eligibility requirements; select a sample of the awards to subrecipients and perform procedures to verify that the subrecipients were eligible and amounts awarded were within funding limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare awards to the approved application/plan requirements and funding limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment title, definition, and thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Title to equipment acquired by a non-Federal entity with Federal awards vests with the non-Federal entity. Equipment means tangible nonexpendable property with useful life > 1 year and acquisition cost of $5,000 or more per unit (lower limits may be established by entity policy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify entity policy on capitalization thresholds and ownership rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use, records, inventory, safeguarding, and maintenance of equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment shall be used in the program which acquired it or, when appropriate, other Federal programs; equipment records shall be maintained; a physical inventory shall be taken at least once every two years and reconciled to the equipment records; an appropriate control system shall be used to safeguard equipment; and equipment shall be adequately maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test inventories, reconcile records to physical existence, inspect safeguards and maintenance practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition and reimbursement for equipment with FMV > $5,000
rubrics_metrics.description: When equipment with a current per-unit fair market value in excess of $5,000 is no longer needed for a Federal program, it may be retained or sold with the Federal agency having a right to a proportionate amount of the current fair market value. Proper sales procedures should provide for competition and result in the highest possible return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For disposals, verify appropriate sales competition, calculation of agency share, and reimbursement to awarding agency as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real property use, approval for alternate use, and disposition instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Real property acquired with Federal awards shall be used for the originally authorized purpose as long as needed; with written approval it may be used in other Federally-sponsored projects with consistent purposes; the entity may not dispose of or encumber title without prior consent and must request disposition instructions when no longer needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain awarding agency disposition instructions and verify compliance with sale, transfer, or retention rules including reimbursement or compensation to agency for Federal share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of equipment property records
rubrics_metrics.description: Property records shall contain description (including serial number or other identification number), source, who holds title, acquisition date and cost, percentage of Federal participation in the cost, location, condition, and any ultimate disposition data including date of disposal and sales price or method used to determine current fair market value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace selected purchases to property records and verify completeness of record fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical inspection of sampled equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a sample of equipment identified as acquired under Federal awards from the property records and physically inspect the equipment including whether the equipment is appropriately safeguarded and maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include observation of location, condition, and security controls as part of physical inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification and recording of equipment dispositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the amount of equipment dispositions for the audit period and perform procedures to verify that dispositions were properly classified between equipment acquired under Federal awards and equipment otherwise acquired, and that dispositions were properly reflected in the property records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test disposition transactions for correct classification and timely update of property records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement testing for equipment dispositions above threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: For dispositions of equipment acquired under Federal awards with a current per-unit fair market value in excess of $5,000, test whether the awarding agency was reimbursed for the appropriate Federal share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify computation of Federal share and evidence of reimbursement or other disposition instructions compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing dispositions of real property
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine real property dispositions for the audit period and ascertain such real property was acquired with Federal awards; for dispositions, perform procedures to verify that the non-Federal entity followed the instructions of the awarding agency which will normally require reimbursement to the awarding agency for the Federal portion of net sales or fair market value at time of disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace real property sales/transfers and check remittances or compensation to awarding agency as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for acceptable matching (cost sharing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable matching: are verifiable from the non-Federal entity's records; are not included as contributions for any other Federally-assisted project or program unless specifically allowed; are necessary and reasonable for proper accomplishment of project objectives; are allowed under applicable cost principles; are not paid by the Federal Government under another award except where authorized; are provided for in the approved budget when required; conform to other applicable provisions of the A-102 Common Rule and OMB Circular A-110 and award terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test sources, documentation, allowability, and non-duplication of matching contributions; corroborate valuation of in-kind and third-party contributions per OMB cost principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of matching/cost sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Matching or cost sharing includes requirements to provide contributions (usually non-Federal) of a specified amount or percentage to match Federal awards; may be in the form of allowable costs incurred or in-kind contributions (including third-party in-kind contributions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the form of matching required and relevant valuation/documentation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of level of effort (LOE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Level of effort includes requirements for (a) a specified level of service to be provided from period to period, (b) a specified level of expenditures from non-Federal or Federal sources for specified activities to be maintained from period to period, and (c) Federal funds to supplement and not supplant non-Federal funding of services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine applicable LOE metrics (hours, expenditures, persons served) and trace reported measures to supporting records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of earmarking
rubrics_metrics.description: Earmarking includes requirements that specify the minimum and/or maximum amount or percentage of the program's funding that must/may be used for specified activities, including funds provided to subrecipients; may also specify types of participants covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify earmarking thresholds and scopes in laws/regulations/award terms before testing compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit objectives for matching, level of effort, and earmarking
rubrics_metrics.description: Matching — determine whether the minimum amount or percentage of contributions or matching funds was provided; Level of Effort — determine whether specified service or expenditure levels were maintained; Earmarking — determine whether minimum or maximum limits for specified purposes or types of participants were met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tests to evaluate each objective using samples, reconciliations, and examination of supporting documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested procedures for testing matching
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform tests to verify that the required matching contributions were met; ascertain the sources of matching contributions and test that they were from an allowable source; test records to corroborate values placed on in-kind contributions in accordance with OMB cost principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate matching tests with allowable costs/cost principles testing; sample transactions and corroborate third-party valuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested procedures for LOE maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the required level of effort and perform tests to verify that the level of effort requirement was met; verify only allowable categories of expenditures or other effort indicators were included and that categories were consistent year to year; verify amounts used in computation were derived from books and records and non-monetary indicators were supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test trends, source documents, and consistency of categorization across periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested procedures for supplement-not-supplant
rubrics_metrics.description: Ascertain if the entity used Federal funds to provide services they were required to make available under law and were also made available by funds subject to a supplement-not-supplant requirement; identify federally-funded services and perform procedures to determine whether federal program funded services that were previously provided with non-Federal funds and whether total level of services increased in proportion to the Federal contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare service levels before and after federal funding, review historical funding sources for the services, and document conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested procedures for earmarking compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the applicable percentage or dollar requirements for earmarking; perform procedures to verify that amounts recorded in the financial records met the requirements; when minimums are required, select transactions supporting the specified amount or percentage and test classification; when maximums are required, review other accounts for misclassified transactions that may cause exceedance; when participant-count requirements exist, select samples to verify proper classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sampling and classification testing to detect misclassifications and to verify counts used to meet numeric participant requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation and liquidation within period of availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal awards may specify a time period during which the non-Federal entity may use the Federal funds; a non-Federal entity may charge to the award only costs resulting from obligations incurred during the funding period and any pre-award costs authorized; obligations must be liquidated within required time (A-102 §.23; OMB A-110 §.28).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For entities subject to A-102, liquidation typically must occur within 90 days after the end of the funding period unless the Federal agency extends the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit objective: period of availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether Federal funds were obligated within the period of availability and obligations were liquidated within the required time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tests to validate obligation and liquidation dates relative to award period and any program-specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested procedures to test period of availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Review award documents and regulations to determine availability period; test a sample of transactions charged to the Federal award after the end of the period to verify that underlying obligations occurred within the period and liquidation was made within the allowed time; test transactions recorded during the period to verify obligations occurred within the period; select a sample of adjustments and verify they relate to transactions that occurred during the period of availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine contracts, purchase orders, receiving reports, and payment records to validate obligation and liquidation timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement policies must conform to Federal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: States and governmental subrecipients of States shall use the same policies and procedures used for procurements from non-Federal funds and ensure every purchase order or contract includes any clauses required by Federal statutes and executive orders and their implementing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain entity procurement policies and verify conformity with A-102 Common Rule or OMB A-110 as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local government/institution-specific procurement procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Local governments and Indian tribal governments which are not subrecipients of States will use their own procurement procedures provided they conform to applicable Federal law and standards in the A-102 Common Rule; institutions of higher education, hospitals, and other non-profits shall follow OMB Circular A-110 procurement procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which procurement rules apply to the entity type and test compliance accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension and debarment prohibitions and certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-Federal entities are prohibited from contracting with or making subawards under covered transactions to parties that are suspended or debarred; covered transactions include procurement contracts for goods or services equal to or in excess of $100,000 and all nonprocurement transactions. Contractors receiving awards >= $100,000 and all subrecipients must certify that the organization and its principals are not suspended or debarred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify required certifications were obtained or alternatively check the GSA List of Parties Excluded From Federal Procurement or Nonprocurement Programs for sampled contractors/subrecipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit objectives for procurement and debarment
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether procurements were made in compliance with A-102 Common Rule, OMB Circular A-110, and other procurement requirements specific to an award, and whether the non-Federal entity obtained the required suspension and debarment certifications for covered contracts and subawards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design procurement and certification tests, including file reviews and GSA list checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement file content and procurement process controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Written selection procedures should require solicitations to incorporate a clear and accurate description of technical requirements, identify requirements offerors must fulfill, and include all factors to be used in evaluating bids or proposals; there should be a written policy pertaining to ethical conduct; contract files should document the significant history of the procurement, including rationale for method of procurement, selection of contract type, contractor selection or rejection, and the basis of contract price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine policies and a sample of contract files for required documentation, ethical policies, and evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full and open competition, justification for limited competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that procurements provide full and open competition; examine documentation supporting any rationale to limit competition and ascertain if the limitation was justified (see § .36 and § .43/.44 references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review solicitation processes, bidder lists, justification memos, and approvals for sole-source or limited competition procurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost or price analysis and approvals for procurements exceeding thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that appropriate cost or price analysis was performed in connection with procurement actions, including contract modifications, and that the awarding Federal agency approved procurements exceeding $100,000 when such approval was required (e.g., noncompetitive negotiation, single bid, other than low bidder, 'brand name' specifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect analysis documentation and evidence of required federal approvals for higher-risk procurement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: State law compliance for procurements subgranted by States
rubrics_metrics.description: Test a sample of procurements to ascertain if the State's laws and procedures were followed and that the policies and procedures used were the same as for State funds (applies to States and subgrants issued by States).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare procurement actions to applicable State law/procedures and ensure parity with State-funded procurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing for suspension and debarment on all non-Federal entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Test a sample of procurements and subawards and ascertain if the required suspension and debarment certifications were received for subawards and covered contracts or check the GSA list to ascertain if contracts were awarded to suspended or debarred parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document certifications or GSA EPLS checks performed for sampled vendors and subrecipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program income definition and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Program income is gross income received that is directly generated by the Federally-funded project during the grant period; may deduct costs incident to generation to determine program income. Includes fees for services, use/rental of property acquired with grant funds, sale of commodities fabricated under a grant, payments of principal and interest on loans made with grant funds. Excludes interest on grant funds (covered under Cash Management), rebates/credits/discounts/refunds (covered under Allowable Costs), interest earned on them, and proceeds from sale of equipment or real property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify revenue streams and classify whether they meet the program income definition or belong to other compliance areas (cash management, cost principles, property).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for using program income
rubrics_metrics.description: Program income may be used in one of three methods: deducted from outlays, added to the project budget, or used to meet matching requirements. Unless specified otherwise, program income shall be deducted from program outlays. For R&D by colleges/universities and other non-profits, the default is to add program income to the project budget. Unless regulations or award terms specify otherwise, non-Federal entities have no obligation to the Federal Government regarding program income earned after the end of the grant period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine applicable method from award terms or agency regulations and test accounting/use of program income accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit objective for program income
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether program income is correctly determined, recorded, and used in accordance with the program requirements, A-102 Common Rule, and OMB Circular A-110, as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tests to validate program income determination, recording, and usage consistent with award terms and applicable regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested procedures to identify program income
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the laws, regulations, and provisions of contract or grant agreements applicable to the program to ascertain if program income was anticipated and the requirements for determining or assessing program income; inquire of management and review accounting records to ascertain if program income was received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine fee schedules, user fee scales, prohibitions on fees for certain groups, and accounting records to identify and assess program income.
